abstract:
Recently Neil Ross and Peter Selinger analyzed the problem of approximating $z$-rotations by means of single-qubit Clifford+T circuits. Their main contribution is a deterministic-search technique which allowed them to make approximating circuits shallower.

We adapt the deterministic-search technique to the case of Pauli+V circuits and prove similar results. Because of the relative simplicity of the Pauli+V framework, we use much simpler geometric methods.

specification.problem: Approximate single-qubit z-rotations by Pauli+V circuits using an adaptation of the Ross-Selinger deterministic-search technique, so that approximating circuits are shallower. The abstract says simpler geometric methods suffice.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Problem statement and a minimal approximation-error formulation only. The abstract gives no algorithm details, circuit structure, or measurement protocol, so none are reconstructed.

symbols.domain: Single-qubit unitary generated by Pauli and V gates

equations.label: Approximation criterion
equations.description: Circuit U approximates the target z-rotation to within precision epsilon in some chosen norm.
equations.abstract_quote: approximating $z$-rotations by means of single-qubit Clifford+T circuits
equations.justification: Approximating z-rotations is the stated problem. The precise norm and error metric are assumed because the abstract does not give them.
assumptions: The error norm is not specified in the abstract and is assumed to be an operator-type norm.

registers.name: q
registers.role: Single data qubit on which the Pauli+V circuit U acts to approximate R_z(theta)

specification.initial_state: Arbitrary single-qubit input state; U is a unitary synthesized to approximate R_z(theta), so no specific initial state is required.

steps.description: Fix target angle theta and precision epsilon, and choose an error norm.

Run a deterministic search, adapted from Ross-Selinger and using geometric methods, over candidate Pauli+V unitaries (details not given in the abstract) to find U within epsilon of R_z(theta), preferring shallow circuits.
Output the Pauli+V gate sequence for U and apply it to the qubit q.

specification.measurement: None specified in the abstract. This is a circuit-synthesis problem; any verification would be a computational-basis measurement after applying U, which is an assumption.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical search yields the gate sequence; check the error bound eq_1 classically. No quantum-measurement postprocessing is described in the abstract.
assumptions: The error metric is a standard operator-type distance.
The circuit is a single-qubit gate sequence; the search procedure is classical and its details are unspecified.
Single data qubit register assumed; the synthesis search is classical.
Measurement, if any, is an optional computational-basis readout and is not part of the paper's described result.
Measurement, if any, is an optional computational-basis readout.
missing_information: Definition of the Pauli+V gate set and its algebraic structure
